narrative: The model estimates a 58% chance that you will leave your job, so it treats leaving as more likely than staying; on that basis, your promotion is denied. The strongest signal is your overall work experience: with 11+ years, you are far outside the typical profile of employees predicted to stay, only about 15% of whom have that much total experience. That makes the model see you as more mobile and pushes toward leaving. The second strongest signal is that you report having other job opportunities; among employees predicted to stay, only about 23% say this, so this also pushes toward leaving. The third signal works in your favor: 6–10 years in your current organization is common among stayers and slightly lowers the likelihood of leaving. It was not enough to offset the first two signals. Given this is only a modest majority prediction, the organization should not treat it as certainty. A conversation should review your career path, the external opportunities you see, recognition, support, job stability, and satisfaction, and agree on retention and development steps. You should clarify what would keep you engaged and whether a promotion decision should wait for stronger evidence.
